Two players alternately remove elements from a prefix F[0..R-1]; you may only add an element to your container if it stays non-decreasing, while your friend removes any element to minimise your score. Answer queries (G, R), where G decides whether you may skip turns.

sources.passage:
Adobe Hackathon OA

Problem Statement

You are given an integer N and an array F of size N. Additionally, you are given Q queries. Each query consists of two integers G and R.

Game Type

G determines the type of game:

  • G = 0: You must make a move if a valid move is possible on your turn.
  • G = 1: You can skip your turn any number of times.

Range of Play

R determines the range of elements involved in the game. Only the elements from F[0] to F[R-1] participate in that query. 

F[0], F[1], ..., F[R-1]

Game Rules

You and your friend play alternately, and you play first.

On your turn, you can:

  1. Select any element from the current range.
  2. Remove that element from F.
  3. Add it to a container C.
  4. You may add the element only if C remains sorted in non-decreasing order.

On your friend's turn:

  • Your friend removes any one element from the current range.
  • Your friend plays optimally and tries to minimize your final score.

Important Rule

If G = 0 and it is your turn but there is no element that you can legally add to C, you lose and your score becomes 0.

If G = 1, you may skip your turn even if there is no valid element that can be added.

The game continues until there are no elements remaining in F[0...R-1].

Score

If you successfully continue until the game ends, your score is the sum of all elements in C.

Both players play optimally:

  • You try to maximize your final score.
  • Your friend tries to minimize your final score.

For every query (G, R), determine the optimal score you can guarantee.

Input Format

N Q
F[0]
